entities.summary: James Evan Perry Jr. is an American former professional baseball pitcher. He pitched in Major League Baseball (MLB) from 1959 to 1975 for the Cleveland Indians, Minnesota Twins, Detroit Tigers, and Oakland Athletics. During a 17-year baseball career, Perry compiled 215 wins, 1,576 strikeouts, and a 3.45 earned run average. He won the Cy Young Award in 1970 and was a three-time MLB All-Star. He and his younger brother Gaylord Perry, who were Cleveland teammates in 1974–1975, became the first brothers to both win 200 games in the major leagues, and remain the only brothers to both win Cy Young Awards.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jim Perry's two Cy Young Awards and 215 wins had a significant impact on Major League Baseball, cementing his place among the greatest pitchers of all time. His achievement with his brother Gaylord also marked a historic milestone in baseball.
